citations.quote: Then: (a) There is a unit vector $w\in H$ with $\langle\rho w,w\rangle\ne\langle\sigma w,w\rangle$. (b) For the rank-one orthogonal projection $P:=T_{w,w}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), whose spectral projection-valued measure assigns $P$ to the Borel set $\{1\}$, the two scalar laws of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b) satisfy $$\mu^{P}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\langle\rho w,w\rangle,\qquad \mu^{P}_{\sigma}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P)=\langle\sigma w,w\rangle,$$ so the bounded sharp observable $P$ assigns different outcome probabilities to $\rho$ and $\sigma$. (c) For every unit vector $w$ and every self-adjoint trace-class $T$ one has $|\operatorname{tr}(TT_{w,w})|\le\|T\|_1$; in particular $|\langle\rho w,w\rangle-\langle\sigma w,w\rangle|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b). **(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number.

The declared outcome law of the model is therefore a probability measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, not a formal weight attached to eigenvectors. (b) **Mixtures.** If $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a statistical mixture of preparations with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, the series converging absolutely: the outcome law of a mixture is the weighted average of the outcome laws, with classical weights. (c) **Exact values.** For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the probability of the exact value $\lambda$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))$; it is zero for every preparation whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it equals the trace weight of the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$, with $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=1$ for every unit eigenvector $u$. (d) **Spectral support.** $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$: outcomes outside the spectrum of the observable have probability zero. (e) **No density and no discreteness are asserted.** The postulate asserts that $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets and does not assert that it is a density with respect to Lebesgue measure or a finite or countable sum of point masses; the operational object named there is the probability of a declared Borel set, such as a finite-resolution bin, not the value of a density at a point ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (iii)).

This proves the statement, and the assertion involves no measurement procedure beyond the model's outcome law.
